sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Greg Myre
articles.description: Ballistic missiles tore into five districts of the Ukrainian capital before dawn Saturday. President Trump is now walking back a promised boost to Ukraine's missile defense systems.
articles.title: Overnight Russian barrage kills nine in Kyiv, as air defense struggle with U.S. continues

articles.author: Miguel Macias
articles.description: The pro-immigration leader is facing backlash at home and abroad after roughly 60,000 people crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave.
articles.title: Spain's Pedro Sánchez was a hero of migrants. After Ceuta, he faces his biggest challenge

articles.author: Kamala Thiagarajan
articles.description: It's a bold new experiment and it's already won a prize. Residents in a jam-packed slum, many of them living in one-room tin shacks, help design their apartments in a brand new building.
articles.title: How these slum dwellers went from one-room shacks to beautiful new apartments

articles.author: Sydney Lupkin
articles.description: The FDA is poised to render a decision on Moderna's mRNA-based flu shot, which could be the first of its kind to market. The decision is expected to reverberate throughout the biotech industry.
articles.title: FDA weighs a new kind of flu shot based on technology RFK Jr. has questioned

articles.author: Isabella Gomez Sarmiento
articles.description: This summer marks a moment of transition in the Grateful Dead's long, strange trip: the first in many years where there is no clear center of the band's universe. Where do Deadheads go from here?
articles.title: Dead After Death

articles.author: Jane Arraf
articles.description: Residents of the ancient town of Nabatiyeh in southern Lebanon have endured wars in the past, but the latest conflict with Israel is testing the limits of their endurance.
articles.title: Lebanese who fled the Israeli invasion visit to see what's left

articles.author: Chiara Eisner
articles.description: Thousands of unaccompanied immigrant children are set to lose legal representation. The federal contract that pays for legal access expired Friday.
articles.title: More than 25,000 children lose previous legal protections, as federal contract ends

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The death toll in Spain's Ceuta border crisis with Morocco has climbed to 67. They included some who drowned and some who were killed in a stampede to cross a breakwater barrier.
articles.title: Death toll in Spain border crisis reaches 67 as tens of thousands cross back in to Morocco

articles.author: Huo Jingnan
articles.description: OpenAI and Anthropic say their models broke into other companies' systems during testing, raising security concerns amid a heated debate over how to regulate AI.
articles.title: Why did OpenAI's and Anthropic's AI models hack other companies?

articles.author: Hope McKenney
articles.description: In June, the Department of Defense disinterred the remains of an unidentified WWII soldier who had been buried in Sitka, Alaska for decades. Now, they'll try to confirm who he is.
articles.title: Over 81,000 U.S. soldiers are missing from past wars. One may soon be identified

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Community members concerned about loss of community green space and areas of cultural importance. Follow updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Yolngu leaders in north-east Arnhem Land have announced a powerful new Dilak Land Council, declaring land rights are “coming home” to traditional owners, AAP reports.
On a national stage at the Garma festival, revered elder Djawa Yunupingu told leaders, politicians and visitors from across the country on Saturday real power must sit “fully into the hands of landowners”.
There will be a new land council in Arnhem Land and it will be called the Dilak Land Council, and it will be the power for our future.
Icac should be allowed to go through its processes free of political interference, free of commentary from politicians, and be allowed to run its course.
Writing the review into the 2022 election, we specifically said that each division needs to make sure that its constitution is fit for purpose and that that its membership is match-fit to fight elections.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: concept images of controversial 2032 Brisbane Olympics precinct revealed

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Police chief says the shooter is among the dead in ‘very chaotic scene’ near busy shopping area in Twin Falls
A shooting at an In-N-Out Burger restaurant in southern Idaho on Saturday afternoon left multiple people dead and others injured, police said.
The shooter was among the dead, Twin Falls police chief Matthew Hicks said in a news conference. Police were still trying to determine the shooter’s identity and motive.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shooting at In-N-Out Burger restaurant in Idaho leaves multiple people dead, police say

articles.author: Reuters in Moscow
articles.description:
More than 20 people injured in explosion near Italian restaurant on Saturday night, authorities say
A homemade bomb carried by a woman killed three people and injured at least 21 in ⁠an explosion near a restaurant in central Moscow on Saturday evening, authorities said.
The explosion occurred just before 8pm close to an Italian restaurant located in one of Moscow’s seven Stalin-era skyscrapers at Kudrinskaya ​Square, the police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Moscow restaurant bombing kills three people as device carried by woman explodes

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Disclosure from 2021 investigation marks first time a bank has formally tied money-laundering concerns to Donald Trump
Capital One Financial hit back on Friday against a lawsuit over its ⁠decision to close the Trump ⁠Organization’s bank accounts ​years ago, stating that it did so after a review by anti-money-laundering experts.
The disclosure marks the first time a bank has formally tied money-laundering concerns to Donald Trump’s family business. Capital One is seeking to dismiss the case by casting doubt on claims of illegally debanking – or denying services on religious or political grounds – the Trump Organization.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Capital One says it closed Trump Organization’s accounts after anti-money-laundering review

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
In Oregon and Washington, low humidity and powerful winds have put officials on alert for wildfire spread
A heatwave scorching the western US region has elevated the risk of hazardous fire conditions particularly in parts of Oregon and Washington, where low humidity and powerful winds have put officials on alert for wildfire spread.
The National Weather Service has forecast blistering temperatures through early next week that could climb from 110F to 120F across the south-west. In the Pacific north-west, highs reaching into the 90s are expected in the days to come.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Heatwave scorching western US ups risk of hazardous fire conditions

articles.author: Josh Halliday and Aletha Adu
articles.description:
PM argues for codified model of decentralisation that would fundamentally change centuries-old workings of state
Andy Burnham has said his programme of devolution strengthens the case for a written constitution for the UK, a move that would fundamentally alter the workings of the state that have developed over centuries.
The prime minister has long believed the UK’s “antiquated” political system needs a dramatic overhaul if opportunity is to be shared equally across the country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Devolution plans strengthen case for written UK constitution, says Burnham

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Veteran actor best-known for playing Salvatore ‘Big Pussy’ Bonpensiero, friend of Tony Soprano who becomes FBI informant
Vincent Pastore, a veteran actor who played mobsters and tough guys, and was best-known for playing Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero on The Sopranos, has died. He was 80.
Bob McGowan, who had managed Pastore since his run on The Sopranos, told the Associated Press that he learned of his death Saturday from another client and actor on the show, Vincent Curatola.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sopranos actor Vincent Pastore, known for playing mobsters and tough guys, dies aged 80

articles.author: Dan Collyns in Lima
articles.description:
Aircraft crashes into field after departing from nearby city of Pisco, according to local authorities
Police in Peru report that 13 people, among them foreign tourists, have been killed in a plane crash in southern Peru, near the Nazca Lines.
Local authorities in Nazca confirmed that 11 tourists and two pilots died when the Cessna Grand Caravan crashed in Pueblo Viejo, approximately 4 miles (6km) from the city of Nazca and roughly 12km from the Nazca Lines site.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tourist plane crashes during flight over Peru’s Nazca Lines, killing 13

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
Gavin Newsom says new pay floor of $17.40, set to become highest of any US state, will go into effect on 1 January
California governor Gavin Newsom announced that the state’s minimum wage will rise to $17.40 next year, a ay floor set to become the highest of any US state.
The pay bump will go into effect starting 1 January, Newsom announced on Friday. The state’s current minimum rate is $16.90. In a news release, Newsom touted the move as a salve for working families amid high living costs and took a jab at the Trump administration.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: California announces minimum wage increase as governor taunts Trump

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll in London and Sam Jones in Madrid
articles.description:
Divisions remain in the bloc over mass crossing of migrants into Spanish territory in north Africa
The EU is to hold an urgent meeting of interior ministers on Tuesday amid continued divisions in the bloc over the arrival of more than 50,000 migrants in the Spanish territory of Ceuta in north Africa.
The decision was taken by officials representing EU member states and Frontex border agency experts at what was described as a “sobering” meeting on Saturday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU to hold urgent meeting of interior ministers on Tuesday over Ceuta crisis

articles.author: Taz Ali (now); Emily Mackay (earlier)
articles.description:
‘Not a single person reached mainland Spain or rest of EU,’ says European Commission president, after Spanish PM condemned ‘selfish, polarising’ reaction of some countries
Back to Ukraine, where nine people were killed in Kyiv this morning from a Russian missile and drone attack.
Damage was reported in seven districts of the capital, according to Ukrainian officials, with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying fires broke out across the city and residential buildings, a school and infrastructure sites were hit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU offered Spain support ‘from first moment’ of Ceuta crisis, says von der Leyen, after Sánchez hits out – Europe live

articles.author: Donna Ferguson and agencies
articles.description:
At least five taken to hospital and about 300 evacuated in strongest quake to hit southern Italian region in 40 years
At least 26 people have been injured after a 4.7-magnitude earthquake rocked a region near Naples, in southern Italy.
The quake, which occurred at 7.46pm on Friday night, caused power outages, disrupted public transport and damaged a pier in Campi Flegrei, the site of Europe’s largest volcanic crater.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Dozens injured as earthquake hits near Naples in seismic swarm

articles.author: Geneva Abdul
articles.description:
Other members of expedition led by world-renowned climber on Broad Peak also died, climbing company says
A world-renowned Nepali mountaineer and former UK Special Forces member has died after being among 11 climbers caught in a deadly avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak.
Nirmal Purja was killed leading an expedition of 10 other people on the world’s 12th-highest mountain when an avalanche struck at around noon on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Top mountaineer Nirmal Purja confirmed dead after 11 hit by avalanche in Pakistan

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Britons move away from trend of grey paving and pristine lawns in an embrace of colour, with lavender a top choice
If you manage to spot a garden in bloom this summer, beyond the strips of bleached and torched grass, there may be one colour you see more than any other: purple, the horticultural hue of the season.
Plants such as lavender, salvias and catmint are in vogue, according to the Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which conducted extensive research into the colours Britons best love to see in their gardens.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Purple reign: how shade became British gardeners’ favourite

articles.author: Kevin Rawlinson
articles.description:
Some in Dover say their town is being exploited by content creators and politicians, but others claim there is a genuine problem
If you believe rightwing influencers and politicians, Dover and the wider Kent coast has been the site of an “invasion” for years now. And, for an online audience of millions, they and their camera crews have been the vanguard in the nation’s defence.
Indeed, if you believe all you see on the algorithms of amateur Channel watchers, the shadow home secretary, Chris Philp, braved a hail of French gunfire as he took to the water in a fishing boat this week; an attempt by the French authorities, he suggested, to deter him in his mission of highlighting the small boats crisis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: On the ground in the English seaside town rightwing influencers say is being ‘invaded’

articles.author: Jakub Krupa
articles.description:
The measure will impact people travelling by plane or boat between the two countries
Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez is now in Ceuta, accompanied by interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska.
He first visited the Tarajal border crossing, and is now talking to officials from local authorities, border and police services.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Italy says it’s temporarily suspending EU Schengen arrangement with Spain after 60,000 migrants reach Ceuta – as it happened

articles.author: Sean Ingle in Glasgow
articles.description:
Tarona Taafaki makes history in women’s 75kg category

All boxers eliminated in semis receive bronze medals

A boxer has made history for ⁠Tuvalu by winning the tiny Pacific island nation’s first Commonwealth ⁠Games medal without winning a single fight.
Twenty-year-old Tarona Taafaki, ⁠one of five entrants in the women’s 75kg category, received a bye to the semi-finals where she lost on an unanimous points decision to India’s Lovlina Borgohain on Friday. At Commonwealth Games, all boxers eliminated in the semis receive bronze medals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Boxer secures Tuvalu’s first Commonwealth Games medal without winning a bout

articles.author: Lauren Cochrane
articles.description:
Some have called it ‘S&M’, but partnership with Ann Summers is less a scandal than another step in a century of evolving underwear trends, experts say
The news that Marks & Spencer is selling Ann Summers crotchless knickers on their website has been greeted – as might be expected – with outrage online, being described as everything from “tawdry” to “S & M”.
But it could be this is just the latest evolution in what the UK’s biggest underwear retailer has available for the smalls drawer. In recent years, the store has sold vastly different options through its own products, ranging from full-brief knickers to thongs, period knickers and those that can be used by women who wear stomas. The introduction of other brands in clothing came five years ago, with underwear included. Ann Summers – which is selling bras and chemises as well as knickers on the M&S website – lines up alongside lingerie brands including Pour Moi and Calvin Klein.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Knickers in a twist: why M&S selling crotchless underwear isn’t as outrageous as it seems

articles.author: Denis Campbell
articles.description:
Alcohol is embedded in profession where long hours, loneliness and lobbying are the norm, report finds
Parliament is “Britain’s last alcohol-soaked workplace” where MPs are offered free drinks as early as midday despite alcohol-related scandals, a report has revealed.
Drinking is commonplace and some MPs have had their stomachs pumped after consuming so much alcohol that they ended up in hospital, one disclosed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘MPs have had their stomachs pumped’: concerns over ‘alcohol-soaked’ culture in Westminster

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Labour veteran is said to relish role that requires careful negotiation of Trump and impending G20 leadership
Extraordinarily, given the importance of geopolitics, the office of foreign secretary has sometimes appeared a consolation prize in British politics, perhaps reflecting the transfer of responsibility to Downing Street or the Cabinet Office.
That is not how Ed Miliband views the job. His allies say suggestions that he nurses resentment after he was deprived of the chance to be chancellor misunderstand his grasp of the policy challenges ahead. “Ed has an immense appetite to get things done and is relishing being in this job,” one says. “Ed will be a policy-driven foreign secretary.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU relations, climate crisis and Gaza: why Ed Miliband is fired up by Foreign Office challenges

articles.author: Graham Readfearn  Environment and climate correspondent
articles.description:
Helicopter surveillance finds dead and dying greater crested terns off South Australian coast as H5 virus spreads

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

More than 80 dead and sick birds seen on rocks off the South Australian coast are suspected to be the first mass mortality event from the deadly H5N1 bird flu virus, only six weeks after the disease arrived in Australia.
Authorities reported on Saturday that helicopter surveillance had revealed 49 dead greater crested terns on Baudin Rocks, near Robe, as well as 35 more sick terns.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: First Australian mass mortality event suspected as deadly bird flu virus rapidly escalates among native birds

articles.author: Agence France-Presse in Singapore
articles.description:
Two members given ‘stern warnings’ after concert and barred from returning, with band also excluded from performing in Singapore again, say authorities
British trip-hop band Massive Attack has been barred from performing in Singapore after an investigation found two members unfurled a Palestinian flag during a concert, police said.
Singapore, known for its tough laws on public speech and assembly, bans the open display of all foreign flags, national emblems or banners without a permit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Singapore bans Massive Attack for showing Palestinian flag, breaching ban on foreign emblems

articles.author: Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
Petrol now costs more than $1.90 a litre in every capital city, with diesel expected to exceed $2.40 a litre

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Petrol prices could surpass $2 a litre and diesel $2.40 in coming days, after the government’s 16-cent discount ends on Sunday.
The 32-cent per litre reduction in fuel excise, introduced in March at the peak of the fuel price spike, was halved to 16 cents in July.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Petrol prices on track to top $2 a litre as Bowen sounds death knell for fuel excise relief

articles.author: Robert Mackey and agencies
articles.description:
Treasury secretary’s notepad, photographed by Reuters on Friday morning, prompts questions over US plans
During a cabinet meeting at Camp David on Friday, the US treasury secretary Scott Bessent carelessly revealed plans for the US to buy $5bn-$10bn ⁠in Japanese yen in a scribbled “to do” list left visible to a Reuters photographer.
The image, taken over Bessent’s shoulder during a portion of the meeting open to journalists, showed a Camp David notepad with the underscored words “To Do” followed by “Buy Japanese Yen (JPY) $5-10 bil”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bessent ‘to-do’ list shows proposal for US to buy $5bn-$10bn of Japanese yen

articles.author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
articles.description:
Indian conglomerate offsets earnings from Carmichael mine to report $340.6m loss, after promising billions in taxes and royalties

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Indian conglomerate Adani will pay no company tax despite generating almost $1bn in revenue from coal mining in Queensland over the past year.
Financial accounts show the Carmichael thermal coal operations used large costs – including production and related party logistics expenses – to offset its $963.5m revenue in the 12 months to 31 March. This resulted in a recorded $340.6m loss for the year, erasing its tax bill.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Adani to pay no company tax despite $1bn revenue from Queensland coalmine

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Body of William Standish discovered in Teton mountains as investigators say fatal fall likely cause of death
A 28-year-old Australian hiker who lost contact with his family while hiking the Continental Divide Trail between Yellowstone and Grand Teton national parks in Wyoming has been found dead, according to authorities.
The man, identified as William Standish, was discovered by rescuers on Wednesday morning in the Wigwams, a series of rocky peaks on the west slope of the Teton mountain range, the Teton county coroner said. Investigators say it was likely he suffered a fatal fall.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Missing Australian hiker found dead in Wyoming, officials say

articles.author: Lucy Campbell (now); Yassin El-Moudden, Tom Ambrose, Taz Ali and Adam Fulton (earlier)
articles.description:
The agreement is a ‘great breakthrough’, the president says in response to media questions

Trump claims agreement for ‘complete disarmament’ of Hamas in Gaza but support uncertain

Saudi Arabia prepares sea and possible land offensive against Houthis

Al Jazeera reporter Hani Mahmoud has reported the mood in Gaza this morning following news of Hamas’s potential disarmament.
Palestinians have heard repeated statements about their fate in the three years since the current war began between Israel and Hamas, so last night’s announcement by Donald Trump wasn’t met with any particular joy or celebration. “There is scepticism and cautiousness among Palestinians,” Mahoud writes from Gaza City in the north of the Strip.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Middle East crisis: Trump says ‘Israel is very happy’ with Gaza peace plan but doesn’t say if withdrawal or Hamas disarmament comes first – as it happened

articles.author: Sam Jones in Madrid, Angela Giuffrida in Rome and Jakub Krupa
articles.description:
Pedro Sánchez decries ‘violation of territorial integrity’ as other EU countries criticise Madrid over incident
At least 57 people have died trying to reach the Spanish enclave of Ceuta after as many as 50,000 migrants entered the tiny territory from Morocco in what Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, called “a violation of Spain’s territorial integrity”.
The huge influx, which took place over the course of just 24 hours, overwhelmed the city of 85,000 people, triggered a political crisis for Madrid and led to a mixed reaction from other EU countries, including calls for Spain to be suspended from the Schengen free-movement zone.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least 57 people die as tens of thousands cross to Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco

articles.author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
articles.description:
António Guterres says strengthening El Niño will help push the world’s climate crisis into ‘uncharted territory’
India’s monsoon is in danger and hotter, drier conditions are forecast across much of the world as a stronger El Niño weather system is taking hold, weather experts have warned.
António Guterres, the UN secretary general, said the strengthening El Niño was “adding fuel to a planet already on fire” and pushing the world into “uncharted territory”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s monsoon rains in danger as UN chief warns planet is ‘on fire’

articles.author: Hannah Harris Green in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Injectable PrEP drug holds promise but investment in HIV prevention has declined dramatically worldwide

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email 

New innovations in HIV prevention could dramatically reduce the number of new HIV cases around the globe, but US foreign aid cuts will mean that those that most need the new medication will be unable to access it, according to experts at the Aids 2026 Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
One year ago, the World Health Organization recommended that governments around the world prioritize expanded access to lenacapavir, an injectable version of the HIV prevention medication PrEP that requires only two injections annually. PrEP, which also comes in the form of daily oral medications and bimonthly injections, is 99% effective in preventing sexually transmitted HIV for people who take it consistently.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: HIV prevention drug could reduce cases globally but USAID cuts prevent access, say experts

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Julian Borger; produced by Annie La Vespa and Angus Neale; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin
articles.description:
Donald Trump has declared a breakthrough in negotiations over the disarmament of Hamas in Gaza and the withdrawal of Israeli forces, but Israeli government officials have voiced scepticism over the deal.
Lucy Hough speaks to Julian Borger, the Guardian’s senior international correspondent – watch on YouTube
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hamas agrees to Trump’s plan to disarm in Gaza – The Latest

articles.author: Peter Beaumont and Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad
articles.description:
Rescuers say four bodies found in search for team caught in Broad Peak avalanche, after trackers showed rapid descent
The world-renowned Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja – a former British special forces member – is among 11 climbers caught in a deadly avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak.
The Alpine Club of Pakistan said “seven climbers have been spotted via aerial drone footage” adding that “their identities and condition cannot yet be verified”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: World-renowned climber Nirmal Purja among 11 struck by avalanche on Pakistan mountain

articles.author: William Christou in Beirut
articles.description:
Energy prices have soared again since fighting between US and Iran resumed two weeks ago as conflict spreads across Middle East
Iran has said it struck two tankers trying to pass through the strait of Hormuz under the escort of the US military as Donald Trump gathered his cabinet to discuss the stalling war and rising prices as midterm elections in the US loom.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Friday that the “non-compliant oil tankers … were struck and brought to a halt, while four other oil tankers quickly changed course and returned to their previous positions”. The military body said the ships had tried to pass through the strait via an “undeclared route” and under US aerial escort.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran strikes tankers under US escort in Hormuz strait as Trump gathers cabinet to discuss war

articles.author: Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Live, rolling coverage as London’s biggest companies defy Middle East disruption and UK petrol prices rise to around £1.60 per litre, the highest since Donald Trump ordered renewed strikes
The story piquing the interest of the financial press this morning is that of Leopold Aschenbrenner, the AI Wunderkind (he’s German-born) who has been forced to sell off his fund in a fire sale after the AI boom ran out of steam.
The 24-year-old had persuaded a lot of people to give him a lot of money for a hedge fund, after previously working for OpenAI and the FTX Future Fund, a charitable arm of the fraudulent crypto empire of Sam Bankman-Fried, who is now in prison. Aschenbrenner ploughed that money into debt-fuelled bets on artificial intelligence companies, earning huge returns until he found out that stocks can also fall.
The trader dubbed the “Nostradamus of AI” would have been hard-pressed to foresee how quickly his high-flying hedge fund would run into trouble.
The firm’s rapid downward spiral is a familiar tale, as Silicon Valley and Wall Street once again threw their weight behind a bright-eyed but untested investor who promised this time would be different. “Everybody always wants to find the next golden child,” said one longtime hedge fund executive. “It just keeps happening.”
In less than 24 hours — which included a conversation between Griffin and Aschenbrenner — Griffin’s Citadel hedge fund reached out to Situational Awareness and snapped up the investments at a discount, according to a person familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified citing private information.
It was a startling reversal for Aschenbrenner, a former researcher at OpenAI who – before starting his hedge fund roughly two years ago — had no previous investment experience. His fledging firm has watched its assets plunge from $45bn at the start of July to about $10bn.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: FTSE 100 on track for best month since first US attacks on Iran five months ago – as it happened

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Cape Coast
articles.description:
During visit to Ghana, Sarah Mullally expresses regret and says controversial fund symbolises Christian belief in repentance
At a former British castle where thousands of enslaved Africans were held before being shipped across the Atlantic, the archbishop of Canterbury expressed “lament” for the Church of England’s involvement in transatlantic chattel slavery and reaffirmed her commitment to a controversial £100m fund for affected communities.
Sarah Mullally made the comments during a visit to the Cape Coast castle, a 17th-century fortress built by Swedish traders, but occupied by the Danish and the Dutch, before the British seized it in 1664.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Archbishop of Canterbury vows to support £100m pledge helping communities affected by enslavement

articles.author: Prosper Heri Ngorora in Bunia
articles.description:
As the death toll rises to almost 1,500, and with a vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain potentially still months away, health workers face a battle to slow the outbreak
The latest numbers of confirmed cases of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has made this latest outbreak the fastest growing in the known history of the virus.
At 3,360 confirmed cases, the disease is now affecting people in five provinces in the east of the DRC, with 1,487 deaths recorded, representing an overall case fatality rate estimated at about 45%, according to Congolese health officials. Health responses to the outbreak have been badly hampered by conflict in many of the affected areas.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ebola outbreak in DRC the fastest growing in the history of the virus

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
State department ‘takes full responsibility’ for erroneous, widely shared chart displayed at Aids conference in Brazil
A US government map of Africa mislabeled every country during a state department presentation at a ⁠global conference in Brazil ⁠this week, ​causing a stir among attenders who took screenshots and posted them online.
Reuters viewed a video of the presentation given at the Aids 2026 conference in ⁠Rio de Janeiro, which shows the errant map displayed halfway during a presentation about the state department’s new health agreements.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US government map of Africa mislabels every country at global conference

articles.author: Gavin Blair in Tokyo
articles.description:
Soldiers and emergency teams search damaged shopping centre, paper mill and homes for survivors

Earthquake rocks southern Japanese island of Kyushu – in pictures

The death toll from the powerful earthquake that hit Japan on Tuesday has risen to 30, as the search for survivors trapped in a badly damaged shopping centre, paper mill and collapsed homes across the south-west of the country continues.
The 6.8-magnitude quake, which struck Kumamoto prefecture on the island of Kyushu, injured at least 62 people, according to the prefectural government.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Death toll in Japan earthquake rises to 30 as aftershock and heat hamper rescue efforts

articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now) and Taz Ali (earlier)
articles.description:
Emergency workers are continuing their search for survivors in southern Japan after yesterday’s powerful earthquake 

‘Race against time’: Japan earthquake death toll rises as rescue teams search for missing

An aerial view of a collapsed section of a bridge in the city of Yatsushiro after an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.1 struck Japan’s southern Kumamoto prefecture:
Japan’s Mainichi Shimbun newspaper has been speaking to people at the Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro, where a chimney collapsed on to the site. 

 “I never imagined something like this would happen,” said a 33-year-old man who worked at the factory. “I never thought that the chimney could collapse. I’m worried about the people inside.”

 He was off duty and at home when the earthquake struck, and was unharmed. The names of those rescued and those trapped have not yet been released. “Someone I know might be affected,” he said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rescue teams face ‘race against time’ in search for trapped survivors as death toll in Japan rises to at least 13 – as it happened

articles.author: Olivia Bowden in Toronto
articles.description:
Data shows Canadians have replaced US vacations with other international trips in apparent rebuke to Trump
Canadians spent $3.3bn less on travel to the US in 2025 than in the previous year, as Donald Trump’s hostile policies towards his northern neighbour continue to incur an economic cost, new government data shows.
The research also indicates that Canadians are not bucking travel overall and instead have replaced US vacations with other international destinations, in a rebuke to Trump’s tariff regime and the president’s continued musings on annexing Canada.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canadians spent $3.3bn less on travel to US in 2025 after Trump’s return to office

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad
articles.description:
Local civil rights group alleges authorities removed evidence of killings amid communications blackout
At least 30 people are alleged to have been killed in Pakistan-administered Kashmir in the past two days as part of what has been claimed is a brutal state crackdown that has engulfed the disputed region for weeks.
According to a local civil society group, Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), the Pakistani security services fired on tens of thousands of peaceful protesters, killing 25 people on Monday and five more on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan accused of fatally shooting 30 unarmed protesters in Kashmir

articles.author: Oliver Milman
articles.description:
Three years after Maui wildfires many still struggle with ‘biological, emotional and social consequences’, study says
A spate of ferocious wildfires across North America and Europe, worsened by the climate crisis, has incinerated homes and forests and forced thousands of people to flee. Previous fires suggest the effects of these blazes may linger for years to come.
The current fires and their plumes of smoke can appear to be a temporary, if immediate, crisis. Nearly 1,000 fires have sprung into life in the boreal forests of Canada, causing the evacuation of towns and toxic smoke to waft into major Canadian and US cities, prompting threats of retribution from Donald Trump, who bizarrely accused Canada of “poisoning” his country’s air.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Past fires suggest effects of Europe and North America wildfires may linger for years

articles.author: Facundo Iglesia in Buenos Aires and Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
President also blames Brazil and Mexico and says online critics ‘do not want the ideas of freedom to succeed’
More than a week has passed since Ferran Torres scored the extra-time goal that gave Spain its second World Cup, but – at least for Argentina’s president – the tournament is not over.
Javier Milei has claimed that a coordinated “anti-Argentina campaign” was behind criticism of the country’s team, accusations of racism among its fans and conspiracy theories alleging that Lionel Messi’s side was secretly being favoured by Fifa.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Javier Milei accuses US Democrats of financing ‘anti-Argentina campaign’ at World Cup

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Cockroach Janta party says government has broken promise, with detentions in Delhi, Assam, West Bengal and Bihar
India’s youth-led “Cockroach” movement, whose nationwide protests forced the resignation of the education minister, has accused the government of backtracking on its promise not to act against student protesters and has threatened to restart demonstrations.
The Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which organised mass protests over exam paper leaks and other irregularities, said it had received reports of hundreds of students being detained or “harassed” by police.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach movement threatens to restart protests after mass student arrests

articles.author: Natasha May and Jonathan Watts
articles.description:
From Afghanistan to Taiwan, unprecedented deluge highlights devastating impact of climate breakdown
“It rained for 10 days and 10 nights, non-stop – I’d never seen anything like it,” says Anar Gul, a construction worker who lives in the remote district of Dur Baba in eastern Afghanistan.
The houses in his village are built from stone and mud, which makes them extremely vulnerable to heavy rains. After days of rain, Gul’s kitchen collapsed and his neighbour, Sayed Afsar Sadat, saw a large part of his house completely destroyed. “Rains like this are coming heavier and earlier each year,” says Sadat. “They are destroying the roads and washing away our crops. It’s impacting us directly.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We have lost everything’: extreme rainfall across Asia brings flash floods and typhoons

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Disclosure from 2021 investigation marks first time a bank has formally tied money-laundering concerns to Donald Trump
Capital One Financial hit back on Friday against a lawsuit over its ⁠decision to close the Trump ⁠Organization’s bank accounts ​years ago, stating that it did so after a review by anti-money-laundering experts.
The disclosure marks the first time a bank has formally tied money-laundering concerns to Donald Trump’s family business. Capital One is seeking to dismiss the case by casting doubt on claims of illegally debanking – or denying services on religious or political grounds – the Trump Organization.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Capital One says it closed Trump Organization’s accounts after anti-money-laundering review

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
Gavin Newsom says new pay floor of $17.40, set to become highest of any US state, will go into effect on 1 January
California governor Gavin Newsom announced that the state’s minimum wage will rise to $17.40 next year, a ay floor set to become the highest of any US state.
The pay bump will go into effect starting 1 January, Newsom announced on Friday. The state’s current minimum rate is $16.90. In a news release, Newsom touted the move as a salve for working families amid high living costs and took a jab at the Trump administration.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: California announces minimum wage increase as governor taunts Trump

articles.author: Shrai Popat in Bangor, Maine
articles.description:
Troy Jackson gained the party nomination for Senate, but now he needs to consolidate support to take on Susan Collins
Troy Jackson is ready to move on.
In fewer than 100 days, the new Democratic nominee has to convince Maine voters to send him to the US Senate – and he’s trying to do it without dwelling on Graham Platner, who dropped out of the race after accusations of rape, which he denies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Upheaval in Maine and another 100-day campaign - can Democrats pull it off?

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Truth Social, where Trump’s account is by far the largest, to offer users early access for up to $100,000 per month
Donald Trump is now offering early access to his Truth Social posts in a move that has been seen as corruption benefitting a sitting president.
Trump Media and Technology Group officially rolled out its new subscription-based data service on Saturday, giving paying customers faster, real-time access to Truth Social posts from Trump and other high-profile accounts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump offering early access to online posts in move seen as corruption

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
As Jeanine Pirro moves to drop charges, flawed work by Trump-connected contractor emerges as culprit
Donald Trump’s Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool saga appears to be winding down after prosecutors dropped vandalism charges against former Olympian David Hearn – but not entirely.
On Friday, Trump appointee and US attorney Jeanine Pirro and assistant US attorney Michael ⁠Spence petitioned a judge to dissolve the justice department’s case against Hearn, 67, who had been accused of pool sabotage, and instead blamed the “botched installation” of pool liner materials that caused it peel, and “less than fulsome information” offered by the Department of Interior.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s reflecting pool saga: a timeline of failure and finger-pointing

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
The US administration has struck a warmer tone of late as Ukraine has shown its value as an ally in the Middle East
As leadership pairings go, Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelenskyy is not a match made in heaven.
It is a far cry from the warm rapport and kindred spiritedness that defined Ronald Reagan’s relationship with Margaret Thatcher, or even the guarded pragmatic friendliness Reagan forged with Mikhail Gorbachev to effectively end the cold war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Laura Loomer, Lindsey Graham and the deepening Iran crisis: what’s behind Trump’s reset with Zelenskyy?

articles.author: Timothy Garton Ash
articles.description:
American democrats need a Hungarian-style landslide to overwhelm Trump’s attempts to rig November’s midterm elections
In these days of extreme weather events, it seems odd to say that the US needs a big landslide. But a landslide defeat for President Donald Trump in November’s midterm elections is exactly what is required if the country is to start reversing his deliberate and rapid erosion of its democracy.
The respected Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) Institute at Gothenburg University argues that in 2025 the US saw one of the most rapid declines in liberal democracy on record. “Democracy in the USA,” says its Democracy Report 2026, “is now at its worst in 60 years.” As the imperial republic marks the 250th anniversary of its founding, the danger seen at the very beginning of its constitutional order by anti-federalists such as Patrick Henry – that of an overmighty president abusing his executive power in an attempt to become a new king – has come closer than ever before.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Democrats have one last chance to halt the erosion of US democracy – and it’s less than 100 days away | Timothy Garton Ash

articles.author: Hosted by Carter Sherman , produced by Meg Driscoll, engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Jonathan Menjivar
articles.description:
With Republicans' chances in the midterms looking shaky, Donald Trump is increasingly trying to rewrite the rules that govern US elections. Voting rights groups say he's really laying the groundwork to suppress voters. Trump has already moved to change mail-in voting, but he now wants Congress to pass the Save America Act, which includes strict voter ID restrictions. He's also accused China of interfering in the 2020 election. (Trump didn't back up that claim with evidence.) Host Kai Wright speaks with Garrett Epps, legal affairs editor at Washington Monthly, about the threat to US elections and what voters can do to protect them.

Read Garrett Epps' story in Washington Monthly

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Will the US midterm elections be free and fair? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Julian Borger ; produced by Annie La Vespa and Angus Neale ; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin
articles.description:
Donald Trump has declared a breakthrough in negotiations over the disarmament of Hamas in Gaza and the withdrawal of Israeli forces, but IsraelI government officials have voiced scepticism over the deal.

Lucy Hough speaks to Julian Borger, the Guardian’s senior international correspondent
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Can Trump’s Hamas disarmament plan work and will Israel agree to withdraw from Gaza? - The Latest

articles.author: Judith Levine
articles.description:
Trump’s campaign of repression echoes the red scare. But now the government has bigger ambitions and more powerful tools
There are many parallels between the first McCarthy era, roughly 1946 to 1956, and Trump’s campaign of political repression, his own updated McCarthyism.
Both regimes crafted a monster of quasi-facts and innuendo and fed it with fear: an enemy within, well-organized and financed, secretive and violent, allied with evil foreigners and bent on overthrowing capitalism, democracy and Christian morality. Both used flagrantly unconstitutional means to cleanse the nation of the spectral menace.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: McCarthyism has returned to the United States – and this time it’s even more dangerous | Judith Levine

articles.author: Margaret Sullivan
articles.description:
The conservative columnist Ross Douthat is the network’s latest perplexing hire – but the move is in line with the new leadership
In media circles, this week’s hire of a prominent New York Times columnist as a correspondent for CBS’s 60 Minutes was greeted with disbelief.
The collective response went something like this: “What?!”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No TV experience? At CBS News, that’s no problem | Margaret Sullivan

articles.author: Sunny Patel
articles.description:
Francesca Hong, a candidate for Wisconsin governor, is part of a wave of democratic socialists finding traction with an old idea
In a matter of weeks, Francesca Hong, an unlikely candidate for governor in one of the country’s most heated battleground states, will test a message that is at once radical and, to many, incredibly practical: the government should help pay for childcare.
“When we talk about free childcare, you can connect to folks whether it’s on an economic argument or just purely that it’s the right thing to do for our kids,” said Hong, a democratic socialist running in Wisconsin’s Democratic primary on 11 August. “I always like to remind folks: if we don’t take care of our kids, who’s going to take care of us?”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How free childcare started winning US elections: ‘Overnight, people realized how essential it was’

articles.author: Matt Gurney
articles.description:
The White House fails to understand that Mark Carney and Canada’s regional leaders can’t cave in to the US president: it’s too toxic to voters
• Matt Gurney is a journalist based in Toronto
Though many hate to admit it, Canadians have long wished for more attention from the US. Well, we’re getting it now. And it turns out that President Trump and some of his top supporters in the Maga movement don’t much like us.
The first big hint was when he started talking about annexing us, saying we couldn’t survive without American support. But the most recent example of Trump’s dislike for Canada can be seen in his latest tariff policies. Canada was largely spared the impact of his “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025 by its pre-existing free trade deal with the US (and Mexico), but earlier this month, as expected, the US declined to extend that deal for another 16-year term. It’s now subject to annual renegotiations. Then, last week, the White House announced tariffs as high as 50% on a selection of Canadian products including, for the first time, items previously protected by the trade agreement. The US called it retaliation for Canadian trade practices.
Matt Gurney is a journalist based in Toronto, and co-editor of The Line, an online magazine
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump has singled out us Canadians for special treatment in his tariff war – there is no choice but to get nasty | Matt Gurney

articles.author: Aaron Gell
articles.description:
J Street’s liberal Zionist politics are landing with the Democratic establishment but the electorate may have moved on
When Daniel Biss addressed his supporters after clinching the Democratic nomination in Illinois’s ninth congressional district this past March, he did something politicians rarely do: he paid homage to a lobby group.
“This victory belongs to J Street,” Biss declared.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Aipac’s brand has become toxic. Can this ‘pro-Israel, pro-peace’ rival move in?

articles.author: Owen Myers
articles.description:
The comedian and actor’s new Netflix special is a gleefully absurd take on politics and potty-mouthed humor
Mary Beth Barone knows exactly who will be offended by her new Netflix special. “JK Rowling, Republicans, establishment Democrats, the British, the Irish and Zionists,” she tells me, reading a list from her Notes app. Then there’s “Katy Kats – which is what Katy Perry calls her fans – and male comedians and one specific girl named Tatiana”. When informed that this encompasses over half of the population of the US, she beams.
Barone’s comedy is a delicate balance between sweetness and cynicism. In her standup she’ll adopt a ditzy pose while she tears down morally bankrupt politicians, sends up cis male entitlement or implores her audience to have sex with moderates in the hope of bringing them over to the left. In the past five years, she has edged her way closer to the mainstream with a Comedy Central web-series, a couple of standup spots on Jimmy Fallon’s late-night show, and a podcast co-hosted with her friend Benito Skinner that is so popular it has its own merch line. The past 12 months have seen her career go into overdrive: now she is the co-lead of a wildly popular TV show (Overcompensating, created by Skinner), chats to the A-list on the Golden Globes’ red carpet and sits front row at New York fashion week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mary Beth Barone on provocative jokes, Palestine and manosphere misogyny: ‘It’s hard to stomach that those are my co-workers’

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman , with David Smith and Rachel Leingang . Produced by Suzanne Gaber and Tiara Chiaramonte , edited by Anabel Bacon , engineered by Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
Earlier this year, Congress reached a depressing milestone: 86% of Americans, a record high, disapproved of its job performance. But this summer, there have been some signs that shifts are underway. On the left, House Democrats have just voted in unprecedented numbers to withhold military aid from Israel, and across the country, progressive candidates are running competitive primary campaigns that are energizing a base fed up with the status quo. On the right, Republicans are reeling from the sudden death of Lindsey Graham, the South Carolina senator and one of Donald Trump's staunchest supporters. Mitch McConnell, the former Senate majority leader, remains sequestered following a health scare in June, raising questions of if a changing of the guard might be underway there, too. Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by David Smith, the Guardian's Washington bureau chief and Rachel Leingang, midwest political correspondent, to discuss gerontocracy, transparency, the rise of the Democratic Socialists of America and just how much of an inflection point this summer might be for both parties


This page was amended on 23 July 2026. A previous version misspelled Lindsey Graham. 

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is US Congress finally on the verge of a change? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Sam Levine Zhara Keogh Michael Kalenderian Sarah Bertram
articles.description:
Donald Trump delivered a primetime address to the country on Thursday, claiming that declassified intelligence showed Chinese interference in US elections. The US president revived long-running attacks on election security, despite a US intelligence assessment that found no evidence Beijing altered the 2020 vote, which he lost. The Guardian's voting rights reporter Sam Levine factchecks some of Trump's claims

Trump is invoking foreign election interference to justify his own - Opinion

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fact-checking Donald Trump’s address on Chinese election interference – video

articles.author: Josh Halliday and Aletha Adu
articles.description:
PM argues for codified model of decentralisation that would fundamentally change centuries-old workings of state
Andy Burnham has said his programme of devolution strengthens the case for a written constitution for the UK, a move that would fundamentally alter the workings of the state that have developed over centuries.
The prime minister has long believed the UK’s “antiquated” political system needs a dramatic overhaul if opportunity is to be shared equally across the country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Devolution plans strengthen case for written UK constitution, says Burnham

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Britons move away from trend of grey paving and pristine lawns in an embrace of colour, with lavender a top choice
If you manage to spot a garden in bloom this summer, beyond the strips of bleached and torched grass, there may be one colour you see more than any other: purple, the horticultural hue of the season.
Plants such as lavender, salvias and catmint are in vogue, according to the Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which conducted extensive research into the colours Britons best love to see in their gardens.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Purple reign: how shade became British gardeners’ favourite

articles.author: Kevin Rawlinson
articles.description:
Some in Dover say their town is being exploited by content creators and politicians, but others claim there is a genuine problem
If you believe rightwing influencers and politicians, Dover and the wider Kent coast has been the site of an “invasion” for years now. And, for an online audience of millions, they and their camera crews have been the vanguard in the nation’s defence.
Indeed, if you believe all you see on the algorithms of amateur Channel watchers, the shadow home secretary, Chris Philp, braved a hail of French gunfire as he took to the water in a fishing boat this week; an attempt by the French authorities, he suggested, to deter him in his mission of highlighting the small boats crisis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: On the ground in the English seaside town rightwing influencers say is being ‘invaded’

articles.author: Christopher Harry
articles.description: Continue reading...
articles.title: Christopher Harry on buying an SUV – cartoon

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
The Reform UK leader is keeping a low profile and his approval ratings have sunk since Burnham took office. What’s the outlook for the Clacton byelection?
This time last year, Nigel Farage was making the political weather. His freewheeling weekly press conferences filled a sparse news agenda, setting out eye-catching policies on areas such as crime and immigration. This year? Less so.
The Reform UK leader is expected to hold a press conference in London next week. If so, it would be just his third since May’s local elections and the first in the capital in more than three months. The man who was everywhere now appears to be in hiding.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The lead singer is unavailable’: Is Nigel Farage spending his summer in hiding?

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political Correspondent
articles.description:
Shift from Westminster risks weakening scrutiny as regional titles battle hostility, big tech and ‘news deserts’
Greater support for local media is needed to hold mayors and councils to account under Andy Burnham’s plans for devolution, which would involve a massive transfer of power into local government, publishers have said.
A range of figures involved with local news broadly welcomed new plans unveiled by the prime minister, but said that monetising content, barriers erected by populist politicians and the roles of big tech and the BBC were among the challenges they faced.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Local media needs support if devolution push is to succeed, publishers say

articles.author: Lauren Cochrane
articles.description:
Some have called it ‘S&M’, but partnership with Ann Summers is less a scandal than another step in a century of evolving underwear trends, experts say
The news that Marks & Spencer is selling Ann Summers crotchless knickers on their website has been greeted – as might be expected – with outrage online, being described as everything from “tawdry” to “S & M”.
But it could be this is just the latest evolution in what the UK’s biggest underwear retailer has available for the smalls drawer. In recent years, the store has sold vastly different options through its own products, ranging from full-brief knickers to thongs, period knickers and those that can be used by women who wear stomas. The introduction of other brands in clothing came five years ago, with underwear included. Ann Summers – which is selling bras and chemises as well as knickers on the M&S website – lines up alongside lingerie brands including Pour Moi and Calvin Klein.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Knickers in a twist: why M&S selling crotchless underwear isn’t as outrageous as it seems

articles.author: Denis Campbell
articles.description:
Alcohol is embedded in profession where long hours, loneliness and lobbying are the norm, report finds
Parliament is “Britain’s last alcohol-soaked workplace” where MPs are offered free drinks as early as midday despite alcohol-related scandals, a report has revealed.
Drinking is commonplace and some MPs have had their stomachs pumped after consuming so much alcohol that they ended up in hospital, one disclosed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘MPs have had their stomachs pumped’: concerns over ‘alcohol-soaked’ culture in Westminster

articles.author: Chloe Mac Donnell
articles.description:
Private White VC’s James Eden says PM should not be criticised for wearing a high-quality British-made brand
It has not yet been two weeks since James Eden, the founder of the Manchester men’s clothier Private White VC, saw one of his best-known customers move in to No 10 Downing Street.
In any sane world the man who makes the prime minister’s jackets would be popping open the champagne. His garments have been seen by millions of people and described by journalists all over the world writing about Burnham’s buttoned-down style.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No apologies, no freebies: the man who makes Andy Burnham’s jackets on how to weather a storm

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Labour veteran is said to relish role that requires careful negotiation of Trump and impending G20 leadership
Extraordinarily, given the importance of geopolitics, the office of foreign secretary has sometimes appeared a consolation prize in British politics, perhaps reflecting the transfer of responsibility to Downing Street or the Cabinet Office.
That is not how Ed Miliband views the job. His allies say suggestions that he nurses resentment after he was deprived of the chance to be chancellor misunderstand his grasp of the policy challenges ahead. “Ed has an immense appetite to get things done and is relishing being in this job,” one says. “Ed will be a policy-driven foreign secretary.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU relations, climate crisis and Gaza: why Ed Miliband is fired up by Foreign Office challenges

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Labour politicians say mutualised model puts public in control without adding debt to government’s balance sheet
MPs and mayors close to Andy Burnham have told the prime minister there is a “third way” to gain more control of failing companies, as the row over whether or not to nationalise Thames Water rumbles on.
Burnham is said to be concerned about the increase in government debt that Treasury projections show could be a result of nationalising water companies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Turn failing water firms into not-for-profit cooperatives, MPs and mayors tell PM

articles.author: Anna Isaac
articles.description:
Nigel Farage’s £5m gift, the Cottrell family’s links and donations, and Richard Tice’s business dealings form part of an increasingly clear nexus of relationships
It has been three months since the Guardian revealed that Nigel Farage had accepted a £5m gift from Christopher Harborne, a billionaire donor to Reform UK.
This was not the first story in our continuing investigation. But it has proved the most significant, and the consequences of the disclosure are still being played out.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The tangled financial web at the heart of Reform UK

articles.author: Sarah Marsh Consumer affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Whey protein, a key infant formula ingredient, is in growing demand, partly linked to rising use of weight-loss drugs
The rise of “proteinmaxxing” – a trend in which consumers try to eat as much protein as possible – could lead to higher prices for infant formula, experts warn.
Whey protein, a key ingredient in infant formula, has surged in popularity over the past year as health professionals emphasise the benefits of protein.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Proteinmaxxing’ could lead to higher prices for infant formula, say experts

articles.author: Helena Smith in Athens
articles.description:
Greek police throw entire homicide division at trying to explain fate of 38-year-old Elisabeth-Jane Ross
Two worlds separated by sheets of corrugated iron: one, a tree-lined road, bordered by a park and the home of Greece’s oldest sports club; the other a wasteland of derelict buildings and graffiti-covered walls in what was once a car park.
It is here, on the wrong side of the divide, in Kypseli, a neighbourhood in central Athens, that the body of Elisabeth-Jane Ross was found, inside a suitcase last month.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Who could have done this?’ Mystery over Briton found dead in a suitcase in Athens

articles.author: Agence France-Presse in Singapore
articles.description:
Two members given ‘stern warnings’ after concert and barred from returning, with band also excluded from performing in Singapore again, say authorities
British trip-hop band Massive Attack has been barred from performing in Singapore after an investigation found two members unfurled a Palestinian flag during a concert, police said.
Singapore, known for its tough laws on public speech and assembly, bans the open display of all foreign flags, national emblems or banners without a permit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Singapore bans Massive Attack for showing Palestinian flag, breaching ban on foreign emblems

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Bev Craig succeeds Andy Burnham and wins back support in areas where Reform made gains in May
Labour has stormed to a decisive victory in the Greater Manchester mayoral byelection, seizing back areas that recently fell to Reform UK and the Greens.
Labour’s Bev Craig, the Manchester city council leader, will now succeed Andy Burnham and hold one of the most powerful political positions outside Westminster.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labour wins decisive victory in Greater Manchester mayoral byelection

articles.author: Kevin Rawlinson
articles.description:
Legal challenge to King’s College London research study claimed it could harm participants but was rejected
A clinical trial of drugs that can delay puberty can go ahead after a high court judge threw out a legal challenge on Friday.
Campaigners had launched the attempt to halt the planned research into puberty blockers, to be run by researchers at King’s College London (KCL), on the grounds that they believed it could harm the children taking part.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: High court clears way for clinical trial giving puberty blockers to children

articles.author: Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
Move will end six decades of production in area, as new CEO tries to simplify company and cut debt

Business live – latest updates

BP has put its North Sea oil and gas business up for sale as it looks to end six decades of production from the basin.
The firm announced on Friday morning it had launched a formal process to market its North Sea business for a potential sale. The move comes as BP’s new chief executive, Meg O’Neill, tries to simplify the company and cut its debt levels.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: BP puts North Sea oil and gas business up for sale

articles.author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
articles.description:
Duetting stars surpass record set in 1953, when crooner Frankie Laine hit the top with I Believe
Sam Fender and Olivia Dean have scored the longest running UK No 1 single in history with Rein Me In, beating a record that has stood since 1953.
Back then, the UK singles chart had been running for less than a year and contained just 12 songs when I Believe, a bombastic ballad by US crooner Frankie Laine, hit No 1 and spent a total of 18 weeks on the chart.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sam Fender and Olivia Dean’s Rein Me In breaks 73-year record to become longest-running UK No 1 single

articles.author: Simon Goodley
articles.description:
Multimillionaire Peter Waddell is also found to have been properly dismissed from Big Motoring World for gross misconduct
A multimillionaire used-car salesman was ousted from his £300m company after “a pre-conceived and orchestrated plan” devised by private equity investors that had backed his business, a high court judge has ruled.
Peter Waddell, 60, was forced out as the chief executive of the Kent-based dealership Big Motoring World in 2024 in a coup that resulted in “more-or-less open warfare” at the car seller and caused “unfair prejudice” to the investment company that held Waddell’s majority stake.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Boss of £300m used-car firm was ousted after ‘orchestrated plan’ by investors, judge rules

articles.author: Pippa Neill and Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Emergency crews say situation remains ‘dynamic’ as more than 100 firefighters battle Dunwich Heath blaze
A wildfire near Britain’s biggest nuclear power station has caused “total devastation” to one of the UK’s most important landscapes, as fire crews said the situation remained “dynamic”.
More than 100 firefighters have been battling the blaze on Dunwich Heath, near Leiston, on the Suffolk coast since Wednesday evening. The fire service said on Friday afternoon the situation was stabilising but remained a “major incident” that was “dynamic and potentially changeable”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wildfire near Sizewell nuclear plant causes ‘total devastation’ to Suffolk landscape

articles.author: Peter Apps, Robert Booth, Sarah Ann Harris and Lauren Hurrell
articles.description:
A Guardian investigation has revealed that a political lobbying firm, founded by the former electoral strategist for David Cameron and Boris Johnson, secretly pays journalists to write pieces for British newspapers that are favourable to its clients.
In a practice that appears to create a back door for private companies to influence public opinion, lobbyists for CT Group, which was co-founded by the campaign strategist Lynton Crosby, told an undercover reporter they had paid journalists to place apparently independent stories in newspapers.
In a statement, CT Group said: 'We do not comment publicly on work we do for clients and we therefore cannot respond to the specific allegations you have made.' CT Group said the events had been 'deliberately mischaracterised' and it did not engage the undercover journalist to do anything and did not pay him anything. It said the journalist was looking for work and 'chased us relentlessly over a period of more than six months'


Lobbying giant filmed offering reporter payment for flattering client coverage in national press

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why undercover footage exposing lobbyists raises concerns for journalism – video explainer

articles.description:
More than 100 firefighters have been battling a blaze on Dunwich Heath, near Leiston on the Suffolk coast, since Wednesday evening and the situation is 'stabilising'. About 50 people have been evacuated from their homes and a nearby holiday park, with some being moved to Westleton, where the village hall was turned into a rest centre


Suffolk wildfire near Sizewell nuclear plant ‘stabilising’ after 24 hours

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Evacuees from Suffolk fire reflect on 'incredibly emotional' day – video

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
Scheme brought in up to 500 foreign-trained doctors a year and was seen as example of British ‘soft power’
The NHS has scrapped a longstanding scheme that let overseas doctors boost their skills in UK hospitals and was seen as an example of British “soft power”.
Senior doctors have criticised NHS England’s decision to axe the Medical Training Initiative, under which 400 to 500 foreign-trained doctors were given placements in Britain every year.

articles.title: Medical colleges condemn scrapping of NHS placements for overseas doctors

articles.description:
Water levels across several of Europe’s major waterways have dropped to exceptionally low levels, setting new records in some areas.
Extreme heat exacerbated by the climate crisis is intensifying the drought hitting the continent as record-breaking heatwaves means the hot atmosphere is evaporating water from rivers, lakes, soils and plants quickly.
The Danube has hit the lowest level of water in 30 years in several countries including Hungary, Serbia and Romania, and the Rhine has dropped to its lowest recorded level in some sections and is expected to drop further due to drought


Climate crisis-driven heat ‘sucking soils dry’ as extreme drought hits Europe

articles.title: Record low water levels across Europe reveal mammoth skeletons and forgotten shipwrecks – video

articles.author: Pippa Neill and Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Major incident declared, with Sizewell B power station monitoring blaze and RSPB nature reserve badly hit
Hundreds of people have been evacuated and a major incident declared after a wildfire spread over more than 80 hectares (200 acres) on the coast of Suffolk, just a few miles from the Sizewell B nuclear power station.
The fire – which had been described by one witness as “apocalyptic” – was said to be stabilising on Thursday night. The statement was posted by Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service, which said at least 12 fire crews were remaining overnight in the area.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hundreds evacuated after ‘apocalyptic’ wildfire near Suffolk nuclear power station

articles.author: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent
articles.description:
Union calling for two paid breaks a day in what it says is punishing schedule for Storehouse ‘order an object’ workers
Staff at the V&A’s Storehouse site in east London have voted overwhelmingly to strike in a dispute over what they say are inadequate toilet and hydration breaks.
They will join staff across V&A sites in London who on Wednesday also voted to strike in a wider dispute over pay, working conditions, and the museum having declined to seek living wage accreditation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Staff at V&A site in London vote to strike over toilet and water breaks

articles.description:
Andy Burnham gave a major speech on Wednesday on his plans for a national care service. He sought cross-party consensus on the issue by speaking to the Tories and Lib Dems. But not Reform UK or the Greens. On Thursday, Reform’s Robert Jenrick claimed at a press conference that the prime minister wanted a ‘death tax’. But is that what Burnham set out? articles.title: Will we pay more tax to fund social care? – podcast

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Bank’s wariness about inflationary pressures from the conflict lie behind decision to hold steady at 3.75%

Business live – latest updates

There is a threat of high inflation coming to the UK but only from the conflict in the Middle East, which could keep oil prices high for much longer than was expected when Donald Trump first began attacking Iran.
It is the war that makes the difference between a benign outlook for inflation and one that puts it back on a rising trajectory, senior UK central bankers believe.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Only the Middle East crisis is preventing a drop in UK interest rates

articles.author: Geneva Abdul and Peter Walker
articles.description:
Several councils to stop housing tenants in glass-fronted Britannia Point in London, where tenants were earlier told they could not use air con
As the fourth heatwave of the year hit the UK on Wednesday, Benice Bodah and her three teenage sons braced for more scorching temperatures inside their south-west London home. The two-bedroom flat has a built-in air-conditioning unit, but it has worked only intermittently in the almost three years since the family were placed in temporary accommodation at Britannia Point in Colliers Wood. “It has not been easy, but what can we do?” said Bodah, 48.
Several councils have now agreed to stop housing families in emergency accommodation in the glass-fronted block after the Guardian revealed they had been told they couldn’t use the air-conditioning during heatwaves as it had “not been offered as an amenity” for them. The 19-storey building is owned by Criterion Capital, set up by the billionaire property magnate Asif Aziz. The temporary tenancies can last from weeks to years and are managed separately by letting agencies, including the London-based Aura Assets Management.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Families to be moved out of billionaire-owned tower after suffering without air con

articles.author: Damian Carrington Environment editor
articles.description:
UKHSA estimates 2,877 fatalities during heatwaves in May and June, almost twice that recorded in 2025 season
England is on track to record its highest ever number of heat-related deaths this summer after the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) announced that an estimated 2,877 people had died in the May and June heatwaves.
The record was set in 2022 with 2,985 deaths, and August, traditionally the hottest month, is yet to arrive. The health secretary, Yvette Cooper, said: “My thoughts are with all those who have lost loved ones as a result of the long and intense heatwaves.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: England on track for record heat-related deaths this summer, official data shows

articles.author: Chris Baraniuk
articles.description:
Boom in migrating moth sightings put down to hot weather, strong winds and food scarcity in Europe 
He had just sat down to dinner in the garden when a speedy visitor whizzed by – a “grey lump with orange wings”, recalled Luke Burstow, from Sussex. It was a hummingbird hawk-moth, a flying insect that migrates to the UK from continental Europe and north Africa.
“I was like: ‘Wow!’,” said the software project manager. “I didn’t even know they existed.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Grey lump with orange wings’: hummingbird hawk-moths descend on UK gardens

articles.author: Lauren Almeida and Jillian Ambrose
articles.description:
Environmentalists renew calls for windfall tax to support households after Q2 earnings rise to almost $10bn
Shell has posted its second highest quarterly earnings on record as the energy market surge caused by the Middle East crisis helped to double its net profit to almost $10bn in the three months to June.
Europe’s biggest oil and gas company reported a quarterly profit of $9.8bn (£7.4bn), more than double the figure for the second quarter last year and the highest since its record-high earnings in the months after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shell’s profits more than double after jump in oil and gas prices

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Labour’s Bev Craig expected to win contest that lost column inches to Andy Burnham’s ascent and Reform UK leader’s self-imposed Clacton vote
Voting has begun in the biggest byelection in British political history, with more than 2 million people eligible to choose Andy Burnham’s successor as Greater Manchester mayor.
In normal times, such a large and politically significant byelection would have dominated the headlines for weeks, particularly as senior Labour figures only weeks ago feared losing the prize mayoralty to Nigel Farage’s Reform UK.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Polls open in Greater Manchester mayoral byelection overshadowed by new PM and Farage’s antics

articles.description:
Mitch Winehouse ‘knowingly and deliberately’ made unfounded allegations against Naomi Parry and Catriona Gourlay, judge says
The father of British music sensation Amy Winehouse has been ordered to pay £950,000 (US$1.26m, A$1.82m) to his late daughter’s friends, who he unsuccessfully sued for auctioning the singer’s clothes and other items.
Mitch Winehouse earlier this year lost a case in the high court in London against two of Winehouse’s friends who auctioned dozens of her clothes and other possessions years after her death.

articles.title: Judge orders Amy Winehouse’s father to pay nearly £1m to her friends
